info.name: octo_template QA API
info.description: Requests for the FastAPI service in src/api.py, which wraps QAAgent's agentic retrieval loop over the PDF knowledge base. Start the server first: `uvicorn api:app --reload` from src/, after running `python main.py ingest`.

request.description: Answers a question from the knowledge base. Response schema: {"answer": "<string>"}.
A blank/whitespace-only question is rejected with 422 rather than being sent to Claude.

item.name: Eval questions (sample)
item.description: A cross-section of the fixture eval bank in docs/eval_questions.json -- one per tag (single, trap, table+compute, footnote, figure, multi-hop, cross-doc). Each request's description holds the reference answer and citation so the agent's response can be checked by hand. Requires `python main.py ingest` to have been run against src/tests/fixtures first. Full bank: `python src/scripts/run_evals.py`.

request.description: Reference answer: Solar photovoltaics, solar water heating, and electric vehicles, using UKHLS (Understanding Society), comparing Wave 4 against Wave 10. Burlinson p1, p8.

Reference answer: Nearly half, 47%, citing the Committee on Climate Change (2022). Burlinson p1. Trap: the same page discusses the 2050 net zero commitment, so a retrieval hit on "target" can return the wrong year.

Reference answer: Table 5, p8. Parental occupation plus parental education: HYBRIDEV 48.16% + 18.24% = 66.40%, SOLARHEAT 31.57% + 22.80% = 54.37%, SOLARPV 16.12% + 7.75% = 23.87%. EVs are most shaped by parental background. For solar PV the dominant single factor is instead birth cohort at 49.24%, more than double the entire parental contribution. The 66.40% figure appears nowhere in the paper.
Reference answer: 66 local governments, which a footnote records as 18% of UK councils. Poulter p5, body text plus footnote 4. The percentage is only in the footnote.

Reference answer: Fig. 5, p9 (FTE change at 2033, the peak activity year). Under HP use at 1:1 the "All Other" effects are broadly positive (London +4,388, South East +3,677, North West +2,863). At 4.8:1 they are broadly negative (London -1,457, South East -1,746, North West -1,153). Higher assumed efficiency means a larger energy bill saving but less offsetting expenditure elsewhere in the economy.

Reference answer: Burlinson p8: (a) socioeconomic inequality is highest for those persistently adopting (innovators) and those persistently not adopting; (b) innovators who relinquished their LCTs over time are more likely to have experienced disadvantaged circumstances; (c) more recent adopters (early-adopters) contributed to the reduction in inequality over the last decade, suggesting the low-carbon transition is increasingly being made by more disadvantaged individuals.

Reference answer: Taylor cites Calvillo et al. 2025 (Taylor p3) for the finding that worker and skills shortages are a common challenge in industrial decarbonisation, with average wage rates increasing as different sectors compete for a limited labour pool. That is the Calvillo paper in this fixture set, whose abstract makes the same wage-cost displacement argument for the heat pump rollout.
